# Independent review: reciprocal conditional-fibre diagnostic

REVIEWED_CANDIDATE_SHA256: 91174e4bb7e7d90602ff8e0344d2a483175acdd75ea67bb7844a57bd1a5c32f1
VERDICT: ACCEPT_RECIPROCAL_MEAN_IDENTITY_AND_SPECIFIED_ISOMETRIC_LIFT_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY.

## Findings

R1 follows exactly from evenness of Phi. The normalizations in R2 are
correct: g_a/F_a=p_(at)/p_t, so R_a is a genuine conditional likelihood
ratio and C_t is its covariance/chi-square Gram kernel.

At large t, monotonicity of chi gives 0<R_a<=aB(t)/B(at), whose limit is
one. Since E_t R_a=1, this proves C_t(a,a)->0 without replacing the varying
measure by a limit.

At small t, the complete relative h asymptotic and the reciprocal r
asymptotic give the prefactor 1/(16 sqrt(t)) and the exponential in R7.
The four-density calculation has lambda=1/a+1/b-1 and produces
1/sqrt(ab lambda)=1/sqrt(a+b-ab). Thus R9 and its endpoint integrability
condition lambda>0 are correct.

For a in (1/2,1), the reciprocal target has limit
 a/sqrt(2a-1)-1>0,
while C_t(a,a)->0. A linear isometry, or a contraction from L2(p_t) to
L2(p_(1/t)) fixing 1 and taking the stated R_a to R_(1/a), would send
R_a-1 to R_(1/a)-1 and violate the norm inequality. The direction is
correctly limited; the opposite contraction, defect-bearing transports, and
extra channels are untouched.

This is a diagnostic of one exact reciprocity lift. It makes no V, L_pi,
or RH sign claim and does not treat the non-admissible reciprocal node as an
original negative-shift witness.
